A delayed emit of the model is realised only by a delayed emit of the implementation for the same event and the payload fields the model sets, delivered after the model delay times the time scale; a timer never realises an emit, and an undelayed emit for a delayed one, or the reverse, is violated (reason emits). libuv v1.48.0, linked into the WebAssembly module because the Lean runtime references it, does not affect the result of a call: the core reaches none of its I/O.
The glue between JavaScript and the Lean core (src/core/lean.js, formal/wasm/glue.c, the emscripten-generated exegra-lean.mjs) passes request and reply bytes unchanged and reports failures as errors.
The WebAssembly engine of the host (V8 in Node and Chrome, SpiderMonkey in Firefox) executes the module according to the WebAssembly specification, Memory64 and exception handling included.
